knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2026_lenacapavir"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2026_lenacapavir"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70254> (open access, PMC13093070)
* Authors' code and digitised data: <https://github.com/KleistLab/LenPrEP>
  (GPL-3.0)

Kim et al. built an integrated model of the HIV-1 capsid inhibitor
lenacapavir (LEN): one plasma PK model for oral tablets and for the
subcutaneous (SC) and intramuscular (IM) long-acting formulations, an Emax
effect of plasma LEN on the production of infectious virions, an established
HIV-1 viral dynamics model used to estimate the IC50 from a monotherapy
study, and a branching-process view of the first replication cycles after
exposure that gives the reproduction number, the infection probability and
the prophylactic efficacy against wild-type virus and seven capsid-resistant
mutants. The PK was fitted to published *mean* (or median)
concentration-time profiles by least squares, so it is a typical-value
model: no between-subject variability and no residual error.

# Population

The PK data are 15 single-dose mean profiles digitised from five studies
(Supplementary Table S1): oral tablets of 300, 900 and 1800 mg in healthy
adults (GS-US-200-4071, Study 2); the SC aqueous suspension at 30-450 mg in
healthy adults (GS-US-200-4070, Study 1) and at 20-450 mg in adults with
untreated HIV-1 (GS-US-200-4072, Study 3); the SC PEG/water solution at 309
and 927 mg in healthy adults (GS-US-200-4358, Study 4; the formulation used
twice-yearly in the PURPOSE trials); and a 5000 mg IM ethanol/water solution
with 5% (F1) or 10% (F2) w/w ethanol in healthy adults (Jogiraju 2025, Study
5). Cohorts had 6-20 participants (136 in total); demographics were not
reported. The IC50 was fitted to the mean viral-load decline after single
SC doses of 20, 50, 150 and 450 mg in Study 3 (6 per dose).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Kim_2026_lenacapavir")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `d/dt(depot_oral)` | n/a | Eq. (1) |
| `d/dt(depot)` | n/a | Eq. (2), PIdir(0) = Frac x dose |
| `d/dt(transit1..3)`, `d/dt(central)` | n/a | Eq. (3) and Figure 1A (Erlang input = transit chain) |
| `f(depot_oral)` = Vd / Vd(dose) | n/a | Eq. (3) with the Table 1 caption power law |
| `eta_wt` and the mutant Emax terms | n/a | Eq. (5) |
| viral-dynamics ODEs | n/a | Supplementary Eqs. (S1)-(S8); drug on NT, NM from deposit `ode_complex()` |
| `viral_load`, `d_viral_load` | n/a | Figure 3 caption; volumes from deposit `solve_pd_ode()` |
| `lambda_inf`, `r0_wt`, `rt_*` | n/a | Eqs. (6)-(8); Supplementary Eqs. (S13)-(S18) |
| `phi_*` | n/a | Eqs. (9)-(10), per transmitted virion |
| `lkel` | fixed log(0.0026) | Table 1, ke |
| `lvc` | log(1618) | Table 1, Vd |
| `lka_oral` | fixed log(1.08) | Table 1, ka (Eq. 4) |
| `lvc_oral`, `e_dose_vc_oral` | log(508.16), 0.61 | Table 1 caption |
| `lka_*`, `lktr_*`, `logitfrel_*`, `ntr_*` | see `ini()` | Table 1, kdirect, kindirect, Frac, n per study |
| `pkvar_lower`, `pkvar_upper` | 0.15, 4.0 | Methods "PK Variability" |
| `lic50` | log(1.6) | Results; Table S3 caption |
| `hill` | fixed 2.1 | Methods "Estimation of Antiviral Potency" |
| viral-dynamics constants | see `ini()` | Table S3 and its caption |
| `k_int_plas`, `rna_per_virion` | 50, 2 | Figure 3 caption |
| `v_int`, `v_plas` | 9.6 L, 3.1 L | deposit `solve_pd_ode()` |
| `fc_*`, `fit_*` | see `ini()` | Table S4 |

## Units, and how to dose the model

Time is in hours and doses in mg. `Cc` is plasma LEN in ng/mL; `Cc_lower`
and `Cc_upper` are the paper's PK-variability envelope (0.15 and 4.0 times
the typical concentration, from the PURPOSE 2 trial). The viral-dynamics
rates are per day in `ini()` and are divided by 24 inside the ODEs.

* **Oral tablet:** dose `amt = <mg>` into `depot_oral`, and carry the oral
  dose in `DOSE_LENACAPAVIR_PO_MG` (it sets the dose-dependent oral volume).
* **Injection:** dose the full injected amount **twice** at the same time,
  once into `depot` (direct release) and once into `transit1` (indirect
  release). `f()` gives `depot` the fraction Frac and `transit1` the
  fraction 1 - Frac.
* **Formulation:** all indicators 0 selects the SC PEG/water solution (Study
  4). `FORM_LENACAPAVIR_SCAQ = 1` selects the SC aqueous suspension, with
  `STUDY_GSUS2004072` choosing the Study 3 (1) or Study 1 (0) fit.
  `FORM_LENACAPAVIR_IM_ETOH5` or `FORM_LENACAPAVIR_IM_ETOH10` selects the IM
  solution.

Outputs:

* `viral_load` (HIV-1 RNA copies/mL) and `d_viral_load` (log10 change from
  baseline) come from the viral-dynamics model of a person with untreated
  chronic HIV-1 infection, which starts at its drug-free steady state.
* `rt_<strain>` is the reproduction number of a strain at the current plasma
  concentration, and `phi_<strain>` is the prophylactic efficacy against that
  strain relative to wild-type exposure without drug (Eq. 10), both for
  constant exposure in a virus-naive person. Strains: `wt`, `q67h`, `n74d`,
  `q67h_n74d`, `q67h_t107n`, `m66i_t107a`, `q67h_k70r`, `q67h_k70r_t107n`.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Kim_2026_lenacapavir")

form_cols <- function(ev, form) {
  ev$FORM_LENACAPAVIR_SCAQ <- as.integer(form %in% c("scaq1", "scaq3"))
  ev$STUDY_GSUS2004072 <- as.integer(form == "scaq3")
  ev$FORM_LENACAPAVIR_IM_ETOH5 <- as.integer(form == "im5")
  ev$FORM_LENACAPAVIR_IM_ETOH10 <- as.integer(form == "im10")
  ev
}

# Injections every `tau` hours (n of them), observed on `obs` (hours).
injection_events <- function(dose, form, obs, n = 1, tau = 0, id = 1L) {
  dose_times <- (seq_len(n) - 1) * tau
  ev <- bind_rows(
    tibble(id = id, time = rep(dose_times, each = 2), amt = dose, evid = 1L,
           cmt = rep(c("depot", "transit1"), n)),
    tibble(id = id, time = obs, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
  ev$DOSE_LENACAPAVIR_PO_MG <- 0
  form_cols(ev, form)
}

oral_events <- function(dose, obs, id = 1L) {
  ev <- bind_rows(
    tibble(id = id, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot_oral"),
    tibble(id = id, time = obs, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    as.data.frame()
  ev$DOSE_LENACAPAVIR_PO_MG <- dose
  form_cols(ev, "peg")
}

solve_typical <- function(ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame")
}
```

# Virtual cohort

The model has no random effects, so every simulation below is a single
typical individual per scenario; no virtual cohort is drawn. The paper's
inter-individual range is the fixed 0.15x-4.0x envelope `Cc_lower` /
`Cc_upper`.

# Replicate Figure 1: single-dose PK by route and formulation

```{r pk-sim}
scenarios <- tribble(
  ~panel,                    ~form,   ~dose, ~days,
  "Oral (Study 2)",          "oral",    300,    60,
  "Oral (Study 2)",          "oral",    900,    60,
  "Oral (Study 2)",          "oral",   1800,    60,
  "SC aqueous (Study 1)",    "scaq1",    30,   224,
  "SC aqueous (Study 1)",    "scaq1",   100,   224,
  "SC aqueous (Study 1)",    "scaq1",   300,   224,
  "SC aqueous (Study 1)",    "scaq1",   450,   224,
  "SC aqueous (Study 3)",    "scaq3",    20,     9,
  "SC aqueous (Study 3)",    "scaq3",    50,     9,
  "SC aqueous (Study 3)",    "scaq3",   150,     9,
  "SC aqueous (Study 3)",    "scaq3",   450,     9,
  "SC PEG (Study 4)",        "peg",     309,   364,
  "SC PEG (Study 4)",        "peg",     927,   364,
  "IM 5% ethanol (Study 5)", "im5",    5000,   392,
  "IM 10% ethanol (Study 5)", "im10",  5000,   392
) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(panel, dose, "mg"))

pk_sim <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenarios)), function(i) {
  sc <- scenarios[i, ]
  step <- if (sc$form == "oral") 0.25 else 6
  obs <- seq(0, sc$days * 24, by = step)
  ev <- if (sc$form == "oral") oral_events(sc$dose, obs) else
    injection_events(sc$dose, sc$form, obs)
  s <- solve_typical(ev)
  tibble(treatment = sc$treatment, panel = sc$panel, dose = sc$dose,
         time = s$time, Cc = s$Cc)
}) |>
  bind_rows()
```

```{r fig1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 1B-C of Kim 2026: typical plasma LEN after a single dose, by route and formulation."}
ggplot(pk_sim |> filter(Cc > 0.3),
       aes(time / 24, Cc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Days post-dose", y = "Plasma LEN (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg)")
```

# PKNCA against Supplementary Table S2

Table S2 lists, for each dose, the Cmax and Tmax that the published model
predicts. PKNCA on the packaged model's single-dose profiles reproduces them.
Study 3 was observed for 9 days only, and the paper's model values for it
(Tmax = 9 days at every dose) are the maximum within that window, so the
Study 3 profiles above stop at day 9.

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- pk_sim |>
  mutate(id = 1L, time_day = time / 24) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time_day, Cc)
dose_df <- scenarios |>
  transmute(id = 1L, treatment, dose, time_day = 0)

o_conc <- PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ time_day | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time_day | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE)
nca_res <- as.data.frame(pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose,
                                          intervals = intervals)))

# Supplementary Table S2, "model" columns (Cmax in ng/mL, Tmax in days).
ref_s2 <- tibble(
  treatment = scenarios$treatment,
  cmax = c(21.3, 24.1, 34.3, 3.1, 10.2, 30.7, 46.1, 2.1, 5.2, 15.7, 47.1,
           16.1, 48.2, 176.2, 219.8),
  tmax = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 20.9, 21, 20.9, 20.8, 9, 9, 9, 9, 84, 84, 112.5,
           83.9)
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res |> select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
  reference = ref_s2,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "day")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Single-dose Cmax and Tmax from PKNCA on the packaged model against the",
  "model values of Kim 2026 Supplementary Table S2. * marks a difference",
  "above 20%."
))
```

```{r pknca-check}
sim_cmax <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  select(treatment, cmax_sim = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(ref_s2, by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (cmax_sim / cmax - 1))
# The injectable parameter sets reproduce Table S2 to within 3% at every dose
# (measured -0.6% to +1.0%); F2 and the oral doses are discussed under
# "Assumptions and deviations".
inj <- sim_cmax |> filter(!grepl("Oral|10% ethanol", treatment))
stopifnot(all(abs(inj$pct) < 3))
# The oral power law approximates the per-dose oral volumes of Table 1.
oral <- sim_cmax |> filter(grepl("Oral", treatment))
stopifnot(all(abs(oral$pct) < 20))
```

# Twice-yearly SC and once-yearly IM dosing

Results: with 927 mg of the SC PEG formulation every 26 weeks the
population-average steady-state range is 32-62 ng/mL (Ctrough to Cpeak); the
5 ng/mL threshold for full protection against wild-type virus is reached
within 23 h of the first injection and maintained up to 50.5 weeks after the
last one. Text S1: once-yearly 5000 mg IM (F1) gives 51.40-205.68 ng/mL.

```{r multidose}
tau_sc <- 26 * 7 * 24
n_sc <- 8
sc_obs <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, (n_sc + 3) * tau_sc, by = 24), 23, 24)))
sc_ms <- solve_typical(injection_events(927, "peg", sc_obs, n = n_sc,
                                        tau = tau_sc))
last_sc <- (n_sc - 1) * tau_sc
ss_sc <- sc_ms |> filter(time >= last_sc - tau_sc, time < last_sc)
after_sc <- sc_ms |> filter(time > last_sc)
weeks_above5 <- (after_sc$time[which(after_sc$Cc < 5)[1]] - last_sc) / 168

tau_im <- 52 * 7 * 24
n_im <- 5
im_ms <- solve_typical(injection_events(
  5000, "im5", seq(0, (n_im + 1) * tau_im, by = 24), n = n_im, tau = tau_im
))
last_im <- (n_im - 1) * tau_im
ss_im <- im_ms |> filter(time >= last_im - tau_im, time < last_im)

tibble(
  Quantity = c("SC q26w steady-state trough (ng/mL)",
               "SC q26w steady-state peak (ng/mL)",
               "Cc 23 h after the first SC injection (ng/mL)",
               "Weeks above 5 ng/mL after the last SC injection",
               "IM yearly steady-state trough (ng/mL)",
               "IM yearly steady-state peak (ng/mL)"),
  Paper = c(32, 62, 5, 50.5, 51.40, 205.68),
  Model = c(min(ss_sc$Cc), max(ss_sc$Cc), sc_ms$Cc[sc_ms$time == 23],
            weeks_above5, min(ss_im$Cc), max(ss_im$Cc))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Measured 32.2 / 62.8 ng/mL, 5.0 ng/mL at 23 h, 50.1 weeks; IM 55.5 /
# 200.8 ng/mL. A wrong Vd, ke or PEG release constant moves the SC range by
# tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  abs(min(ss_sc$Cc) / 32 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(max(ss_sc$Cc) / 62 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(sc_ms$Cc[sc_ms$time == 23] / 5 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(weeks_above5 / 50.5 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(min(ss_im$Cc) / 51.40 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(max(ss_im$Cc) / 205.68 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

```{r fig-ss, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Twice-yearly 927 mg SC PEG LEN: typical profile (line) with the paper's 0.15x-4.0x variability envelope (band) and the 5 ng/mL full-protection threshold (dashed)."}
ggplot(sc_ms |> filter(time > 0, time <= (n_sc + 2) * tau_sc),
       aes(time / 24 / 7)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Cc_lower, ymax = Cc_upper), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cc)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Weeks after the first injection", y = "Plasma LEN (ng/mL)")
```

# Replicate Figure 3: viral-load decline after single SC doses

Mean change from baseline in plasma HIV-1 RNA in Study 3, as digitised by the
authors (deposit `Data/PD`), against the packaged model with the Study 3 PK
parameters.

```{r vl-data}
vl_obs <- tribble(
  ~dose, ~day, ~dvl,
  20, 0, 0, 20, 1.0023, -0.0508, 20, 1.9872, -0.2099, 20, 2.9981, -0.4891,
  20, 5.9933, -0.9465, 20, 6.9874, -1.0327, 20, 7.9895, -1.2697,
  20, 9.0003, -1.2966,
  50, 0, 0, 50, 1.0023, -0.0675, 50, 1.9842, -0.4255, 50, 2.9873, -0.7623,
  50, 5.992, -1.4402, 50, 6.9929, -1.5342, 50, 7.9965, -1.6221,
  50, 8.9973, -1.7934,
  150, 0.9997, -0.066, 150, 1.9897, -0.2753, 150, 3.0062, -0.5847,
  150, 5.9926, -1.1094, 150, 6.9933, -1.3157, 150, 7.9941, -1.5068,
  150, 8.9947, -1.7616,
  450, 0, 0, 450, 0.9995, -0.1722, 450, 1.9945, -0.5636, 450, 2.9897, -0.9398,
  450, 5.9916, -1.6799, 450, 6.9977, -1.8467, 450, 7.9933, -1.9468,
  450, 8.994, -2.1379
)

vl_sim <- lapply(c(20, 50, 150, 450), function(d) {
  s <- solve_typical(injection_events(d, "scaq3", seq(0, 20 * 24, by = 6)))
  tibble(dose = d, day = s$time / 24, dvl = s$d_viral_load,
         log10_vl = log10(s$viral_load))
}) |>
  bind_rows()

# Untreated baseline: Table S3 says betaT and betaM were tuned to about
# 4.5 log10 copies/mL.
baseline_log10 <- vl_sim$log10_vl[vl_sim$day == 0][1]
baseline_log10
stopifnot(abs(baseline_log10 - 4.5) < 0.1)
```

```{r fig3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Kim 2026: log10 change from baseline in plasma HIV-1 RNA after single SC aqueous doses in Study 3. Points: digitised means; lines: packaged model."}
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = vl_sim, aes(day, dvl)) +
  geom_point(data = vl_obs, aes(day, dvl)) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste(dose, "mg")) +
  labs(x = "Days post-dose", y = "Change in HIV-1 RNA (log10 copies/mL)")
```

```{r vl-check}
vl_cmp <- vl_obs |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(model = approx(vl_sim$day[vl_sim$dose == dose],
                        vl_sim$dvl[vl_sim$dose == dose], xout = day)$y) |>
  ungroup()
vl_tab <- vl_cmp |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(mean_abs_diff = mean(abs(model - dvl)),
            day9_obs = dvl[which.max(day)], day9_model = model[which.max(day)])
knitr::kable(vl_tab, digits = 2)
# Measured mean absolute differences 0.12-0.42 log10, largest at 150 mg,
# whose observed decline is smaller than at 50 mg (the paper notes the large
# inter-individual variability of n = 6). An IC50 off by 2-fold shifts the
# day-9 decline by about 0.4 log10.
stopifnot(median(vl_tab$mean_abs_diff) < 0.3, max(vl_tab$mean_abs_diff) < 0.5)
```

# Prophylactic efficacy and the mutant selection window (Figures 4-5)

The reproduction number and efficacy outputs are algebraic in the plasma
concentration. Evaluating them on a concentration grid reproduces the
concentration-response relationships of Figures 4 and 5.

```{r conc-grid}
conc_grid <- exp(seq(log(0.05), log(5000), length.out = 600))
vc <- exp(rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta[["lvc"]])
grid_ev <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = seq_along(conc_grid), time = 0, amt = conc_grid * vc / 1000,
         evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  tibble(id = seq_along(conc_grid), time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0L,
         cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()
grid_ev$DOSE_LENACAPAVIR_PO_MG <- 0
grid_ev <- form_cols(grid_ev, "peg")
grid <- solve_typical(grid_ev)

strains <- c("wt", "q67h", "n74d", "q67h_n74d", "q67h_t107n", "m66i_t107a",
             "q67h_k70r", "q67h_k70r_t107n")
grid_long <- grid |>
  select(Cc, all_of(paste0("rt_", strains)), all_of(paste0("phi_", strains))) |>
  pivot_longer(-Cc, names_to = c(".value", "strain"),
               names_pattern = "(rt|phi)_(.*)")
```

```{r ec95}
# Concentration at which a monotone output crosses a target (log-linear).
crossing <- function(x, y, target) {
  i <- which(diff(sign(y - target)) != 0)[1]
  exp(approx(y[i:(i + 1)], log(x[i:(i + 1)]), xout = target)$y)
}
wt <- grid_long |> filter(strain == "wt")
ec95 <- crossing(wt$Cc, wt$phi, 0.95)
full_protect <- crossing(wt$Cc, wt$rt, 1)
c(EC95 = ec95, full_protection = full_protect,
  R0_wt = grid$r0_wt[1])
# Paper: EC95 = 4.7 ng/mL, full protection at 5 ng/mL (Figure 5), drug-free
# R0 about 11.3. Measured 4.75, 4.87 and 11.33.
stopifnot(
  abs(ec95 / 4.7 - 1) < 0.03,
  full_protect > 4.7, full_protect < 5,
  abs(grid$r0_wt[1] / 11.3 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

```{r msw}
msw_paper <- tribble(
  ~strain,             ~lower, ~upper,
  "q67h",                 0.8,   21,
  "n74d",                 1.7,   59,
  "q67h_n74d",            2.5, 1107.6,
  "q67h_t107n",           1.9,  141.6,
  "m66i_t107a",           3.6,  537.2,
  "q67h_k70r",            1.3,  106.8,
  "q67h_k70r_t107n",      0.8, 1142.3
)
msw_model <- lapply(msw_paper$strain, function(s) {
  m <- grid_long |> filter(strain == s)
  tibble(strain = s,
         # mutant overtakes wild type: R_t(mutant) = R_t(WT)
         lower_model = crossing(m$Cc, m$rt - wt$rt, 0),
         # mutant can no longer sustain infection: R_t(mutant) = 1
         upper_model = crossing(m$Cc, m$rt, 1))
}) |>
  bind_rows()
msw <- left_join(msw_paper, msw_model, by = "strain")
msw |>
  rename("Strain" = strain, "Lower (paper)" = lower,
         "Upper (paper)" = upper, "Lower (model)" = lower_model,
         "Upper (model)" = upper_model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = paste(
    "Mutant selection window bounds (ng/mL): Results and Text S1 of",
    "Kim 2026 against the packaged model."
  ))
# Upper bounds are exact algebra on Table S4 (measured within 1.5%); lower
# bounds are printed to one decimal in the paper.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(msw$upper_model / msw$upper - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(msw$lower_model - msw$lower) < 0.1)
)
```

```{r fig5, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Kim 2026 (median phenotypes): reduction in infection risk relative to wild-type exposure without drug. Dark band: average steady-state range with twice-yearly SC LEN (32-62 ng/mL); light band: variability range (4.8-248 ng/mL)."}
grid_mut <- grid_long |> filter(strain != "wt")
ggplot(grid_mut, aes(Cc, phi)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 4.8, xmax = 248, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "grey90") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 32, xmax = 62, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "grey70") +
  geom_line(data = wt |> select(-strain), colour = "black") +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~strain) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Plasma LEN (ng/mL)", y = "Reduction in infection risk (phi)")
```

```{r fig5-check}
phi_at <- function(s, conc) {
  m <- grid_long |> filter(strain == s)
  approx(log(m$Cc), m$phi, xout = log(conc))$y
}
# Results: in the 32-62 ng/mL steady-state range Q67H is fully prevented and
# Q67H+K70R+T107N is barely affected (2-6% median reduction); Q67H+N74D
# 24-27%; M66I+T107A 53-63%.
fig5 <- tibble(
  strain = c("q67h", "q67h_k70r_t107n", "q67h_n74d", "m66i_t107a"),
  at_32 = sapply(strain, phi_at, conc = 32),
  at_62 = sapply(strain, phi_at, conc = 62)
)
knitr::kable(fig5, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  fig5$at_32[1] == 1,
  fig5$at_62[2] < 0.10,
  fig5$at_32[3] > 0.15, fig5$at_62[3] < 0.35,
  fig5$at_32[4] > 0.45, fig5$at_62[4] < 0.70
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Code deposit as a source.** The paper prints the PK structure, Table 1,
  the viral-dynamics equations and constants (Eqs. S1-S8, Table S3) and the
  Emax model, but not how LEN enters Eqs. S7-S8 or the plasma and
  interstitial volumes that convert total-body virus to plasma viral load.
  Both come from the authors' deposited code (GPL-3.0): LEN multiplies the
  infectious-virion production NT and NM by (1 - eta) and the total virion
  output NhatT / NhatM is unchanged, so the remainder becomes non-infectious
  (Methods: LEN "disrupt[s] viral maturation, leading to the production of
  non-infectious viral particles"); Vint = 9.6 L and Vplas = 3.1 L. With
  these, the untreated baseline is 4.44 log10 copies/mL against the "about
  4.5" of Table S3.
* **The deposited PK code is not the published model.** The deposit's PK
  ODE (`ode_system()`) feeds the indirect pathway with a product of a
  decaying depot and an Erlang term of order n, and its `.ini` files hold
  starting values (e.g. Vd = 139 L). That form does not reproduce Table S2,
  whereas Equation (3) with the Table 1 estimates reproduces every
  injectable Cmax in Table S2 to within 1.0% (except F2, below). The model
  follows the paper.
* **Erlang input as a transit chain.** Equation (3) writes the indirect input
  as the Erlang(n, kindirect) density times the indirectly released amount,
  evaluated from each dose time. That is exactly the output of n transit
  compartments with rate kindirect dosed in the first one, which also handles
  repeated injections by superposition, as the paper's numerical method does.
  The model carries three transit compartments and n (1-3 across Table 1)
  selects which one empties into plasma.
* **Route-specific volume.** Equation (3) divides the oral input by the
  dose-dependent Vd(dose) and the injected input by the common Vd, in the
  same concentration equation. The model keeps `central` on the Vd scale and
  applies Vd / Vd(dose) as the relative oral input, which is the same
  equation.
* **Oral volume from the power law.** Table 1 lists fitted oral volumes for
  the three studied doses (13,304, 35,374 and 46,516 L) and gives the power
  law Vd(dose) = 508.16 x dose^0.61 for any dose. The model uses the power
  law, so it also covers the 600 mg oral lead-in of the clinical regimen. At
  the studied doses it gives 16,483, 32,217 and 49,172 L, so the simulated
  oral Cmax differs from Table S2 by -16%, +14% and +5%.
* **IM 10% ethanol (F2) Cmax.** Table S2 lists a model Cmax of 219.8 ng/mL
  for F2, but Table 1's F2 parameters give 179.5 ng/mL (and the F2 Tmax of
  83 days matches Table S2's 83.9). Figure 1C shows both IM formulations
  peaking below 200 ng/mL, consistent with 179.5, so the Table S2 entry is
  taken as a transcription error and the Table 1 values are kept.
* **Figure 3 after day 9.** Over the observed 9 days the model is within
  about 0.25 log10 of the published fit at every dose. After day 9 the
  published curves flatten, whereas the Study 3 PK of Table 1 (three transit
  compartments, Erlang peak near day 27) keeps raising the concentration and
  the decline continues. The deposit's PD fit used different Study 3 PK
  starting values, so Figure 3 may have been drawn with an earlier PK fit;
  the model keeps the Table 1 parameters and the stated IC50 = 1.6 ng/mL.
* **Efficacy per transmitted virion.** The paper averages the infection
  probability over the number of virions transmitted by receptive anal
  intercourse, drawn from the inoculum distribution of Duwal 2016, which is
  not printed. The packaged `phi_*` is the efficacy for one transmitted
  virion (Eqs. 9-10 with n = 1). It gives EC95 = 4.75 ng/mL against the
  paper's 4.7 and the same full-protection threshold, because R_t <= 1 makes
  the infection probability zero for any inoculum size.
* **Time-resolved infection and de novo resistance** (Eqs. 11-14, Figure 6)
  need a backward-in-time solve of the multi-strain extinction-probability
  equations for each exposure time, which an rxode2 forward simulation cannot
  express; they are not packaged. The `rt_*` and `phi_*` outputs give the
  constant-exposure view that defines the mutant selection windows and
  Figures 4-5.
* **Mutant phenotypes** use the Table S4 median fold change and average
  replication capacity; the shaded uncertainty ranges of Figures 4-5 (Table
  S4 minimum-maximum) can be reproduced by overriding `fc_*` / `fit_*` in
  `ini()`.
* **Clearance of free virus.** The viral-load outputs use CL = 23/day
  (chronic infection) and the prophylaxis outputs use 2.3/day (virus-naive),
  as stated in the Table S3 caption.
* **No IIV or residual error.** The model was fitted to mean profiles by
  least squares. The paper's inter-individual range is the fixed
  0.15x-4.0x envelope from PURPOSE 2, packaged as `Cc_lower` / `Cc_upper`.
